clue.text: Reformed faith ultimately neutral

definitions.note: a faith, while LUTHERAN names a follower or the church; the clue reads as an adjective

indicators.note: reformed means made over in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged; the word also serves the definition
ultimately points to the very end of the word it follows, so only its closing letter is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of faith
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church that has gone through the Reformation ends up taking no side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' works twice: it signals the shuffle and, with 'faith', describes the answer, since the Lutheran church came out of the Reformation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lutheran church, founded on Martin Luther's teaching, was the first Protestant body of the Reformation.

clue.text: Aristocrat right to receive monarch

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: what is your right is your due
K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A nobleman is entitled to entertain the sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of hereditary nobleman in the British peerage.

clue.text: Bend after a blow, though dignified

parts.note: taken as written
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U
a gust is a blow of wind

explanation.surface: Someone stoops after being struck yet keeps their dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the bend behind the 'a', then the blow follows; the clue reads 'Bend after a, blow'.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means majestic, venerable and inspiring respect.

clue.text: Scales line to intellectual storehouse

parts.note: Libra is the zodiac sign of the scales
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Weighing equipment lined up against a warehouse of ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of books is where knowledge and learning are kept for readers to draw on.

clue.text: Victory for many aboard the "Endeavour"

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
aboard a ship is on it
an endeavour is a quest

explanation.surface: Captain Cook's ship Endeavour brings a triumph to its large crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make Endeavour look like the name of Cook's ship; it is just a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is a win taken by force, the overcoming of an enemy or obstacle.

clue.text: Shakespearean bird almost put in jail (American)

indicators.note: something put in another thing ends up inside it

parts.note: the can is American slang for jail

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short

parts.note: the oriole is a songbird
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A bird from Shakespeare nearly ends up behind bars in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Coriolanus is a Roman general and the title character of one of Shakespeare's tragedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriolanus is a play by Shakespeare and its hero, so the adjective stands for a Shakespearean figure.

clue.text: Point in time to an expanse of water

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
E for east, a point of the compass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moment in history leads to a stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The point is a compass point, not a moment, and it sits inside the time after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aegean is the arm of the Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey, a large body of sea.

clue.text: Underground sportsmen in Likud upset monkey

indicators.note: in places the earlier words inside the party name that follows
upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, a body of sportsmen
taken as written: Israel's right-wing party
U stands for underground, as in the U-Bahn

explanation.surface: Secret athletes stir up trouble in Israel's Likud party.
explanation.walkthrough: Likud is an Israeli political party; the anagram turns it, with the extra letters, into an obscure animal name.
explanation.definitionFit: The durukuli is the night monkey or douroucouli of South America, a small nocturnal primate.

clue.text: Protective layer for District and Circle? Vice versa

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle
a district is a zone
an instruction to swap the order of the two pieces, giving no letters

explanation.surface: The London Underground's District and Circle lines seek some shielding.
explanation.walkthrough: District and Circle are London Underground lines. 'Vice versa' tells you to put the circle first and the district second.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer in the upper atmosphere shields Earth from harmful ultraviolet radiation.

clue.text: Old woman about to get rhyming family home

definitions.text: Old woman about to get rhyming family home

parts.words: Old woman about to get rhyming family home
parts.note: surface reading: an elderly lady is about to acquire a house for her family, described in verse
setter's reading: the dwelling in the nursery rhyme where the old woman lived with so many children

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme runs 'There was an old woman who lived in a ...', with so many children she didn't know what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, the old woman's large family lives in a piece of footwear, which is their house.

clue.text: Endure transfer: outside left not returned

indicators.note: outside means the shuffled word wraps around the next piece
to transfer is to move things over, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
to have left is to have quit

explanation.surface: A football club must put up with a transfer: their outside left is not coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: Outside left is an old football position, which makes the whole clue read as a sports story.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrequited love is love that is not reciprocated, given back or answered in kind.

clue.text: Propose to maintain king in health

definitions.note: a noun, while the answer is a toast said as an exclamation

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold and support, so one word holds another inside

parts.note: to posit is to propose an idea
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Suggesting the monarch should be kept in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Propose' and 'health' together hint at proposing a toast, which is what the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a Latin-derived drinking toast meaning 'may it benefit you', said like 'your health!'.

clue.text: Holy man eaten by smoother amphibian

indicators.note: something eaten by another is taken inside it

parts.note: a sander smooths wood
a lama is a Buddhist monk of Tibet

explanation.surface: A holy man devoured by a slicker creature from the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The salamander is a lizard-like tailed amphibian, related to newts.

clue.text: Wine and cheese, unopened, to throw away

indicators.note: unopened means its opening has not happened, so the first letter is gone

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
to sling is to throw away

explanation.surface: Wine and cheese still sealed are simply tossed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape from the Rhine region and the white wine made from it.

clue.text: 1 9 /150 = gradient

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the slash cuts into the number before it, so the next number is inserted there

parts.note: the number written as a word
CL is the Roman numeral for 150

explanation.surface: It looks like a sum, a ratio written in figures equalling a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: Gradients are often written as ratios like 1 in 9, which the slash and numbers imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: An incline is a slope, the amount by which ground rises over distance.

clue.text: Convert to the Pony Express, initially

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the letters change order; the word is also the definition

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the first letter of the word before is used

parts.note: the first letter of Express

explanation.surface: Someone becomes a believer in the old Pony Express mail service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pony Express was the American horseback mail service of 1860-61. 'Convert' does double duty as definition and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a newcomer to a religion, someone newly baptised or recently won over.

clue.text: Speaker about to spoil fishing gear

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the following words are read from the end

parts.note: to rot is to spoil
nets are fishing gear

explanation.surface: Someone talking is on the point of ruining the angling tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads naturally as 'on the point of'; split it, and 'about' turns the words round while 'to' is just a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was a Greek herald in the Iliad with a huge voice, hence any loud speaker.

clue.text: Witchcraft: spinning gold in attempt to get notice, finally

parts.note: obi or obeah is West Indian sorcery

indicators.note: in places the spun piece inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: spinning means turned around, so the word's letters run backwards

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Magic is used to make gold whirl, hoping to get noticed at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' belongs to the definition: an obituary is the last notice someone gets.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a published account of someone's life after death, the last write-up anyone receives.

clue.text: Great lover married? Just the opposite

parts.note: Mark Antony, Cleopatra's lover
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Was the famous lover married? Quite the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word with contrary meaning, like hot for cold.

clue.text: Instrument for putting spirit, hot, into excrescence

indicators.note: putting something into another means it is placed inside, signalled with the word into
into marks where the pieces go: inside the word that follows

parts.note: a corn is a hard growth on the foot
rum is a spirit
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A tool for rubbing hot liquor into a growth on the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: An excrescence is an abnormal outgrowth; a corn on the foot is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The crumhorn is a Renaissance woodwind with a curved end, played with a capped reed.

clue.text: Right one in cultured surrounds ã one in a million?

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: surrounds means goes round, so the word for cultured wraps the numeral

parts.note: arty means interested in culture
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A proper person in cultivated surroundings: a rare find indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is something uncommon; the question mark marks the definition as an example-like phrase.

clue.text: Obscure compiler's inconclusive threat

indicators.note: inconclusive means not reaching an end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the compiler speaking of himself would say my
the stick, as in carrot and stick, is a threat

explanation.surface: The crossword setter makes a vague, unfinished threat.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves as the compiler, so 'compiler's' gives the possessive word for me.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystic means having hidden spiritual meaning, mysterious and beyond ordinary understanding.

clue.text: Alternative to dole is cosmic waste

parts.note: to dole out is to mete out
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Life on unemployment benefit is a waste of space.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit; here it is the verb, to hand out.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a piece of space debris burning up as it enters the atmosphere.

clue.text: Ailment induced by Spooner's blast on the French horn?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the next phrase is said with its starts exchanged

parts.note: a toot is a blast on a horn, here a French one

explanation.surface: An illness caused by playing a brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of 'French toot' and you get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trench foot is a condition of the feet caused by long immersion in cold wet mud, common in the First World War.

clue.text: Far from cheerful actor, so they say

indicators.note: so they say means as spoken, so the answer sounds like the word but is spelt differently

parts.note: an actor is one who acts, a doer

explanation.surface: A gloomy performer, according to gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Dour describes someone stern, sullen and gloomy in manner.

clue.text: Measure up to the barrel-bearer

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a yard is a measure of length

explanation.surface: Measuring up for a barrel carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a low cart traditionally used by brewers to deliver casks of beer.

clue.text: Deal with rubbish round about

indicators.note: round means going about the outside, so the word for rubbish encloses the other piece

parts.note: tat is cheap junk
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Handling the junk that's lying around.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a matter or person is to handle or behave towards them in a given way.

clue.text: Year in which eastern nation gets young leader, the nation's backbone

indicators.note: in which says the following pieces go inside the abbreviation for year

parts.note: YR is the abbreviation for year
E for eastern
Oman is a country in Arabia

indicators.note: the leader is at the head, so just the first letter of young is used

parts.note: the first letter of young

explanation.surface: A year in which an Eastern state gets a youthful ruler who becomes the country's mainstay.
explanation.walkthrough: The yeomanry, small freeholding farmers, were traditionally praised as the backbone of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen, the class of small landowning farmers, were long called the sturdy mainstay of English society.
